sense: keep up, keep in good order

evidence: Quint. 1.1.14: cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus
Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to look to, care for, keep up, uphold, maintain, support, guard, preserve, defend, protect” (“the predom. class. signif. of the word”): of a house, a language, a friendship.

terms.gloss: keep, keep up (a state of mind, a custom)
evidence: Hor. Carm. 2.3.1–2: aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem
Cic. Off. 1.104: lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus
Cic. Fam. 13.50.2: sartum et tēctum, ut ajunt
terms.comment: The builders’ phrase for upkeep, “patched and roofed”; Cicero uses it as a saying (ut ajunt) of keeping a friend safe and sound.

evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.17.3: vīlla ūsibus capāx, nōn sūmptuōsa tūtēlā

phrases.latin: ita fīet, ut, cum aequālī cūrā linguam utramque tuērī coeperīmus, neutra alterī officiat
phrases.english: So it will come about that, once we begin to keep up both languages with equal care, neither will get in the way of the other.

phrases.latin: aequam mementō rēbus in arduīs servāre mentem
phrases.english: Remember to keep a level head when things are hard.

phrases.latin: vīlla ūsibus capāx, nōn sūmptuōsa tūtēlā
phrases.english: a house big enough for one’s needs, and not costly to keep up

sources: Lewis & Short: tueor · Lewis & Short: servo · Lewis & Short: retineo · Lewis & Short: sarcio · Lewis & Short: tutela
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. maintain (a building).
